status: NOTHING HAS BEEN RUN. No model or API call was made producing this document; no spend has occurred. Both deliverables are written and tested offline, and remain DC-B1-gated.

decision.scope: (a) re-score all 4,344 stored evidence items + (b) re-adjudicate the FULL gate-forced pool (87 claims) plus the 6 named extras = 93 claims
decision.ceiling_not_forecast: The 87 is the MAXIMUM candidate pool, not a prediction. Actual spend lands below the ceiling; the expected outcome is nearer $4.
zero_cost_outcomes: adjudication only fires for claims the repaired gate actually RELEASES — a claim that does not flip costs $0
claims that remain legitimately gated (genuinely fewer than 2 bearing Tier-1..3 items after scoring) cost $0 — the gate was right, no panel runs
currently-decided claims that the repair newly WITHHOLDS cost $0 — withholding a verdict needs no panel call
decision.why_not_partial: Partial coverage would leave gate-forced claims asymmetrically unadjudicated: which claims got a second look would depend on where the budget stopped rather than on the evidence. That is an M-6 evenhandedness failure — the published corpus would carry two classes of gate-forced Unverifiable, distinguishable only by budget history. The saving is ~$3 and is not worth the asymmetry.
decision.stress_test_basis: chars/4 tokenization 50% low on (a) AND all 93 claims adjudicating at the high per-claim rate: $0.66 + $6.96 = $7.62, still $2.38 under the ceiling
decision.cap_change_reason: $7.40 against an $8.00 cap is only 8% headroom, and a mid-run cap breach is its own incident — a halted job leaves the corpus half-re-adjudicated, i.e. the same evenhandedness problem arrived at by accident. $10.00 gives 35% headroom over the worst case and still fits inside one $20 day.

b1a_rescore.method: exact score_evidence prompt per sid via relevance.score_payload, measured from the stored artifacts, at 4.0 chars/token, priced with hydramind.models.RATE_TABLE_USD_PER_MTOK['claude-haiku'] = (0.80, 4.00) USD/Mtok in/out

pricing_basis.input_chars: len(relevance._SCORE_SYSTEM) + len(relevance.score_payload(claim_text, items)) per sid — the system prompt plus the exact payload score_evidence would send, measured not guessed
pricing_basis.output_chars: REPLY_CHARS_OVERHEAD (16) + REPLY_CHARS_PER_ITEM (46) * len(items) — the fixed {"i", "relevance", "supports"} record per item plus the {"scores": [...]} wrapper
pricing_basis.why_the_per_item_figure_is_low: one line of the payload in and one small JSON record out, amortised across a batched per-sid call — 66 input + 12 output tokens per item at Haiku rates is $0.0001, which is arithmetic, not optimism
caveats: chars/4 is an APPROXIMATION, not a tokenizer run; JSON scaffolding and URLs tokenize worse than prose, so the true input count is plausibly 10-25% higher (even at +50% this line is under $0.70)

the claude-haiku rate-table entry is flagged in hydramind/models.py as a fallback estimate because Haiku is proxy-priced in practice; Haiku is ON-PROXY, so the funded run is LEDGER-TRUE (proxy_lane.proxy_key_spend) and this estimate only has to be good enough to set a cap

b1b_readjudication.per_claim_source: measured full-stack cost/claim of the three NON-RESUMED phase-3 rebuilds (gwbush 0.0642, clinton 0.0744, trump 0.0748); the two resumed legs undercount because banked_cost carries only proxy spend across sessions, not the off-proxy R2/R3 estimate — see carry_forward_obligations

max_candidate_pool_all_gate_forced.note: PINNED. Every currently gate-forced claim could in principle flip once its evidence is scored; each one that does not costs $0.

b1b_readjudication.brief_correction: The brief called this 'the 66 currently gate-forced claims'. 66 is the newly_gated count (claims the rebuild newly gated relative to the published run), summed from the phase3_*_verdict_diff.json files. The count CURRENTLY gate-forced in the rebuilt runs is 87, and 87 is the pinned pool.

fitness_finding_composition: 17 stored run artifacts = 5 published (live on the site) + 5 rebuilt (staged, unpublished) + 7 superseded (retained per archive-never-delete). The A1 finding that every stored run is unfit to gate is stated over all 17, not over the 5 published reports; this spend repairs the rebuilt cohort, which is the one queued for publication.

carry_forward_obligations.statement: The corpus spend total is a MIXED BASIS — proxy spend is ledger-true (the LiteLLM proxy key was billed), off-proxy spend is a list-rate ESTIMATE — and the two RESUMED legs (obama_2014, biden_2022) UNDERCOUNT their off-proxy portion: phase3_rebuild banks only proxy spend in the chunk journal (append_chunk_journal is handed the proxy_key_spend delta), so a resumed session carries the prior leg's proxy cost forward and drops that leg's off-proxy estimate. The DC-6 table reconstructs both legs from the run logs, recovering what the runner's own SPEND line lost — but only down to the last BANKED chunk; both legs died inside the following chunk after its retrieval had already run. The corpus total is therefore a LOWER BOUND on the off-proxy component, and the two resumed runs' per-claim rates must not be used to price future work.
carry_forward_obligations.implemented_in: scripts/dc6_package.py :: SPEND_BASIS_DISCLOSURE — emitted to dc6_review.json (spend.basis_disclosure, spend.cost_basis.disclosure) and to the '6. Spend + provenance' section of dc6_review.md
